newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM's party tops 1st round of Senate election.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM's party tops 1st round of Senate election.

text.p: The centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus fared best in the first round of elections to the new upper house of parliament, the Senate, Czech Television said on Saturday.
With all 81 of the constituencies reporting, ODS won three seats outright, and sent 76 candidates through to a second-round runoff.

The centre-left opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) did not come out on top in any constituency but sent 48 candidates through to a second round runoff next weekend in constituencies where no candidate won more than half of the vote.

The two junior coalition partners, the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL) and the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), have 17 and seven candidates in the runoff respectively, and the opposition Communist Party (KSCM) has four candidates through.
Early results show however that at least 70 of the ODS candidates going into the runoff won the most votes in their constituency in the first round.

Although analysts viewed the poll as the first test since the coalition lost its majority in June lower-house elections, nationwide voter turnout was only 35 percent, clouding any conclusions which might be drawn from the vote.
